Anna is an environmentalist and is studying the impact of deforestation in a pine forest located in a square-shaped region. Anna discovers that the area of ​​the deforested region is decreasing at a rate of $0.4{\text{ km}}^{2}/\text{month}.$ At what rate are the region's diagonals decreasing if the diagonals are $20\text{ km}$ long?

current_example.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14187261/assets/2677121139896da73eca5277c7c23f193467001eabba976cb48b2232f4bcbad6.png)

In a testing facility, a scientist is increasing the diagonals of a simple square at a rate of $12 \text{ mm}\text{/min}.$ At what rate, in squared millimeters per minute, is the area of the square increasing when the length of the diagonal is $6\, \text{mm}?$
current_example.worked_solution:
Let $h$ and $A$ be the length of the diagonals and the area of the square, respectively. Using the Pythagorean theorem, it can be shown that the relationship between $A$ and $h$ is

$$
A = \dfrac{h^2}{2}.
$$

We want to find

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d A}{\textrm d t}.
$$

Differentiating this relationship with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(A) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{h}^{2}}{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}h}(\frac{{h}^{2}}{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}\cdot h.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $h$ increases at a rate of $12\,\textrm{mm/min},$ so

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we want to compute the rate of change of the area when the diagonal has length $h=6.$ Substituting this information into our expression for $\dfrac{\textrm{d}A}{\textrm d t},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =12\cdot 6=72{\text{ mm}}^{2}\text{/min}.\end{aligned}
$$
